title: Tree Height
statement: Return the number of nodes on the longest path from the root to a leaf using recursion. An empty tree has depth 0.
constraints: Tree depth is at most 500 so a recursive Python solution is supported.
Trees are encoded in level order with null gaps.

brute_force_solution:
def tree_max_depth(root):
    level = [] if root is None else [root]
    depth = 0
    while level:
        depth += 1
        level = [child for node in level for child in (node.left, node.right) if child is not None]
    return depth
hints: Depth counts nodes, not edges; the empty subtree contributes zero.
Ask the same question of the left and right child subtrees.
Return 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)); return 0 at a missing node.
Each call solves one subtree. The recursion reaches O(h) frames and visits every node once.
editorial: Use the recursive relationship depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)), with zero for a missing node. Each node is visited once, so time is O(n), and the call stack uses O(h) space for tree height h. The catalog caps depth at 500 so a correct recursive Python solution is tested as recursion rather than rejected by the interpreter's call-stack limit. Broad trees may still contain up to 20,000 nodes. An independent breadth-first oracle verifies the answers.
